# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (v2, Nov 2026)

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Honest starting position
- One person (Morgan): evenings and weekends, good writing, okay Python.
- Budget: up to $2,000 of personal savings this year. Hard cap.
- One volunteer offer (Priya Raman, data analyst, ~5 hrs/week).
- Constraint: Morgan's employment contract (Dorrance, section 7). **Nothing public under Morgan's name
  (posts, letters, press, public comments, website) until Morgan has talked to HR.** The outside-activities
  disclosure is due 30 Nov, so that conversation is due anyway.

## Where a tiny project can actually add value
Big labs and well-funded institutes cover headline capability evals and policy advocacy. A one-to-three-person
volunteer project has a better chance of being useful if it:
1. Does careful, unglamorous **public-good analysis** that others can build on (datasets, maps, write-ups).
2. Is **legible and checkable**: open methods, small claims, nothing overstated.
3. Builds the people (reading group, volunteers) instead of chasing attention.

## Chosen focus for the next 3 months: "Eval Gap Map"
A structured, open dataset of published AI safety and dangerous-capability evaluations covering what they
measure, who runs them, how often they're reported in model cards and system cards, and **which risk areas
have little or no measurement.** Deliverables:
- `evalmap/` dataset (CSV) + schema + methodology note.
- A short write-up of the 3–5 biggest measurement gaps. Submit to Alignment Commons (call for posts)
  **only after HR clearance**, or have it published under the project name if HR prefers.
- Optionally, after that, a prototype eval for one gap (Python, small compute; Compute Commons credits).

Why this: it matches Morgan's stated idea ("evals for something nobody is measuring"), suits Priya's skills,
it's cheap, it can be finished, and it informs both research and funding decisions.

## Secondary
- **Reading group** (monthly, private, from the meetup contacts). Cheap, builds the people.
- **Emberfall rapid grant** (closes 30 Nov): apply for a modest amount to fund the Eval Gap Map + prototype.
  Draft in `grants/emberfall-rapid-2026.md`. Morgan must be the named applicant and sign, so Morgan submits it.

## Explicitly not doing right now
- Signing open letters, press quotes, public comments, social posts, or publishing the website. These wait
  for HR clearance. Drafts are prepared where there's a deadline.
- Spending beyond small, confirmed amounts.

## Decision log
- 2026-11-16: Adopted v2 strategy. Old/ material set aside per Morgan.

# Eval Gap Map

Goal: an open, checkable catalogue of AI safety and dangerous-capability evaluations, and an analysis of
which risk areas are under-measured.

## Schema (`evals.csv`)
| column | description |
|---|---|
| eval_id | short slug |
| name | eval/benchmark name |
| maintainer | org or authors |
| first_published | YYYY-MM |
| source_url | paper / repo / page |
| risk_area | one of the taxonomy below (multiple allowed, `;`-separated) |
| measures | capability / propensity / control / interpretability / societal |
| access | open / gated / private |
| reported_in_model_cards | names of frontier model or system cards that report results, `;`-separated |
| last_known_use | YYYY-MM |
| notes | free text |

## Risk-area taxonomy (draft, to be revised)
cyber-offense; bio/chem uplift; autonomous replication & resource acquisition; AI R&D automation;
deception & strategic underperformance (sandbagging); situational awareness; persuasion & manipulation;
power-seeking / goal misgeneralisation; oversight evasion / monitor subversion; collusion between AI agents;
long-horizon agentic reliability; societal / labour / concentration-of-power; honesty & calibration;
privacy & data exfiltration; other.

## Method
1. Seed list from model/system cards of major frontier releases (2024–2026), major eval suites, and survey papers.
2. Two-person coding of risk_area for each item; disagreements logged in `disagreements.md`.
3. Gap score per risk area = (# evals) × (fraction reported in model cards). Treat it as a rough signal, not a ranking.
4. Every row needs a source_url. No unsourced claims.

## Status
- [ ] Taxonomy agreed
- [ ] Seed list (target: 80–150 rows)
- [ ] Coding pass 1
- [ ] Gap analysis draft

# DRAFT: Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant proposal
**Status: draft for Morgan to review, edit, and submit. Not submitted.** Deadline: 30 Nov 2026.
The named applicant must be Morgan (accountable and signs the agreement). Check with Dorrance HR first (disclosure due 30 Nov).

---

## Eval Gap Map: finding what frontier AI safety evaluations don't measure
**Applicant:** Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold (independent project)
**Amount requested:** $8,000 · **Duration:** 4 months (Dec 2026 – Mar 2027)

### What we will do
Labs, governments and third-party evaluators now publish many safety and dangerous-capability evaluations,
but nobody keeps a single, open, sourced record of *which risks are being measured, how often results are
actually reported, and where the gaps are.* We will build that:

1. **An open dataset** (target 100+ evaluations) with a sourced record for each: maintainer, risk area,
   what it measures (capability vs. propensity vs. control), access level, and which frontier model and system
   cards report it.
2. **A gap analysis** naming the 3–5 risk areas with the least measurement relative to their importance,
   published openly with the methodology.
3. **One prototype evaluation** for the most tractable gap, released as open code with clear limitations.

### Why it matters
Evaluations increasingly gate deployment decisions and feed proposed rules (e.g. incident reporting).
Unmeasured risks get no attention in those decisions. A public gap map helps funders, evaluators and
policymakers point effort where it's missing, and it's cheap to keep updated.

### Why us
Morgan Hale: [one or two sentences about your background, writing, and Python].
Priya Raman (volunteer, to be confirmed): data analyst, ~5 hrs/week, will run the data collection and coding.
We're small and say so. The project is scoped so that a two-person team can finish it and others can check it.

### Milestones
- Month 1: taxonomy + 100-row seed dataset, double-coded.
- Month 2: gap analysis draft; external review by 2–3 people from the safety community.
- Month 3–4: prototype eval + final write-up; dataset released under CC-BY.

### Budget
| item | USD |
|---|---|
| Research assistance stipend (Priya, ~60 hrs @ $50) | 3,000 |
| Compute / API credits for prototype eval | 2,000 |
| Applicant time (partial, ~40 hrs) | 2,000 |
| Expert review honoraria (3 × $250) | 750 |
| Hosting, domain, misc | 250 |
| **Total** | **8,000** |

### Risks
- Overlap with existing efforts: Month 1 includes a check for this; if a good map already exists, we'll
  contribute to it rather than duplicate it.
- Volunteer time: dataset scope scales down cleanly.

### What we will do
Labs, governments and third-party evaluators now publish many safety and dangerous-capability evaluations,
but nobody keeps a single, open, sourced record of *which risks are being measured, how often results are
actually reported, and where the gaps are.* We will build that:

1. **An open dataset** (target 100+ evaluations) with a sourced record for each: maintainer, risk area,
   what it measures (capability vs. propensity vs. control), access level, and which frontier model and system
   cards report it.
2. **A gap analysis** naming the 3–5 risk areas with the least measurement relative to their importance,
   published openly with the methodology.
3. **One prototype evaluation** for the most tractable gap, released as open code with clear limitations.

### Why it matters
Evaluations increasingly gate deployment decisions and feed proposed rules (e.g. incident reporting).
Unmeasured risks get no attention in those decisions. A public gap map helps funders, evaluators and
policymakers point effort where it's missing, and it's cheap to keep updated.

### Why us
Morgan Hale: [one or two sentences about your background, writing, and Python].
Priya Raman (volunteer, to be confirmed): data analyst, ~5 hrs/week, will run the data collection and coding.
We're small and say so. The project is scoped so that a two-person team can finish it and others can check it.

### Milestones
- Month 1: taxonomy + 100-row seed dataset, double-coded.
- Month 2: gap analysis draft; external review by 2–3 people from the safety community.
- Month 3–4: prototype eval + final write-up; dataset released under CC-BY.

### Budget
| item | USD |
|---|---|
| Research assistance stipend (Priya, ~60 hrs @ $50) | 3,000 |
| Compute / API credits for prototype eval | 2,000 |
| Applicant time (partial, ~40 hrs) | 2,000 |
| Expert review honoraria (3 × $250) | 750 |
| Hosting, domain, misc | 250 |
| **Total** | **8,000** |

### Risks
- Overlap with existing efforts: Month 1 includes a check for this; if a good map already exists, we'll
  contribute to it rather than duplicate it.
- Volunteer time: dataset scope scales down cleanly.
